plan.contextChunk: This figure presents the mass spectrum of chloroethane as a bar-line plot on a pale beige field. The vertical axis reads "Relative abundance (%)" and runs from 0 to 100 with labeled ticks every 20 units; the horizontal axis, labeled "m/z" and followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, spans 10 to 70 with tick marks every 5 units. Inline text near the top center identifies the sample as "CH3CH2Cl" with "MW = 64.5". Each ion is drawn as a thin vertical line whose height encodes its abundance. The densest group sits between about 25 and 30, where three tall lines rise to just above 90 percent and to roughly 85 and 75 percent, with shorter lines beside them and a small cluster near 35 to 37. A medium line near 49 reaches about 25 percent, with a shorter one near 51. At the far right a line at 64 climbs to the full 100 percent and carries the label "M (64)", while a line at 66 reaching about 30 percent is labeled "M + 2"; several short lines fall between 62 and 65. Setting those two labeled lines side by side lets the reader take their height ratio directly, roughly three to one — the signature of an element present as two isotopes in that natural abundance.

interactionPlan.concept: In a mass spectrum, peak position (m/z) identifies fragment masses while peak height gives relative abundance, and the M / M+2 pair at 64 and 66 in a roughly 3:1 height ratio is the signature of one chlorine atom's natural 35Cl:37Cl isotope ratio.

y-axis labeled 'Relative abundance (%)' spanning 0 to 100 with ticks every 20
inline text 'CH3CH2Cl' and 'MW = 64.5' near top center
cluster of tall sticks at m/z 26-29 (heights roughly 28, 75, 91, 85) with shorter neighbors
small sticks near m/z 35-37
medium stick at m/z 49 (~25%) with a shorter one at 51
base-peak stick at m/z 64 at 100%, labeled 'M (64)'
stick at m/z 66 at ~30%, labeled 'M + 2'

highlight bracket connecting the M and M+2 peaks with their ~3:1 ratio annotation (appears on click)

interactions.teaches: The M (64) and M+2 (66) peaks are the same molecular ion carrying 35Cl versus 37Cl, so their ~3:1 height ratio directly reflects chlorine's natural isotope abundances and reveals that the molecule contains one Cl atom

demo_steps.title: Reading the axes
demo_steps.narration: Hover over the tall sticks near m/z 28-29: each line is one ion, its position gives its mass-to-charge ratio, and its height gives its relative abundance. The cluster around 28 is the dominant fragmentation product.

demo_steps.title: The molecular ion pair
demo_steps.narration: Click the M (64) peak: the M and M+2 lines highlight together with their height ratio. 64 is chloroethane with 35Cl; 66 is the same molecule with 37Cl.

demo_steps.title: The 3:1 chlorine signature
demo_steps.narration: The M peak stands about three times taller than M+2 because natural chlorine is ~75% 35Cl and ~25% 37Cl. Seeing an M/M+2 pair in a 3:1 ratio in any spectrum is instant evidence of one chlorine atom.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The M and M+2 peaks separated by 2 mass units in a ~3:1 height ratio are the fingerprint of a single chlorine atom, because the peak heights mirror the natural 35Cl:37Cl abundance ratio.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Stick spectrum on a pale beige field; thin black vertical lines, no bars. Tallest cluster around m/z 26-29 (max ~91%), isolated medium peak at 49, base peak at 64 reaching 100% labeled 'M (64)' with the label placed above-right, and a ~30% peak at 66 labeled 'M + 2'. Formula 'CH3CH2Cl' and 'MW = 64.5' as plain inline text upper-middle. Magenta arrow after the m/z axis label. On click of either labeled molecular peak, draw a bracket or paired highlight (e.g. magenta) over the 64 and 66 sticks with a '~3:1' annotation between them; on hover, show a small tooltip with m/z and % values while dimming all other sticks to ~30% opacity.

authoredContext:
The fact that some elements have two common isotopes gives their mass spectra a distinctive appearance. Chlorine, for example, exists as two isotopes, 35Cl and 37Cl, in roughly a 3: 1 ratio. In a sample of chloroethane, three out of four molecules contain a 35Cl atom and one out of four has a 37Cl atom. In the mass spectrum of chloroethane (the figure we see the molecular ion (M) at m/z = 64 for ions that contain a 35Cl and another peak at m/z = 66, called the M + 2 peak, for ions containing a 37Cl. The ratio of the relative abundance of M: M + 2 is about 3: 1, a reflection of the isotopic abundances of chlorine.

Mass spectrum of chloroethane.

The mass spectrum of chloroethane with two peaks at m / z 64 and 66, labeled M and M + 2, on a 3 to 1 height ratio.

In the case of bromine, the isotopic distribution is 50.7% 79Br and 49.3% 81Br. In the mass spectrum of 1-bromohexane (the figure) the molecular ion appears at m/z = 164 for 79Br-containing ions and the M + 2 peak is at m/z = 166 for 81Br-containing ions. The ions at m/z = 135 and 137 are informative as well. The two nearly equally large peaks tell us that the ions at those m/z values still contain the bromine atom. The peak at m/z = 85, on the other hand, does not contain bromine because there is not a large peak at m/z = 87.

discrepancies: the source figure's distinctive tan/beige gradient background fill is absent — the generated plot area is plain white, noticeably changing the figure's overall look
the source has a complete rectangular plot frame (top and right border strokes); the generated chart draws only the left and bottom axes
the step-2/3 isotope-pair bracket and '≈ 3 : 1 / ³⁵Cl : ³⁷Cl' annotations are additions not present in the source (acceptable as interaction content, but they extend beyond the static figure)
evaluation.notes: Stick positions, heights, axis ranges, and all four key labels (M (64), M + 2, CH₃CH₂Cl, MW = 64.5, plus the magenta m/z arrow) faithfully reproduce the chloroethane spectrum, and the 3-step player with the M/M+2 isotope-pair highlight teaches the 3:1 chlorine signature correctly; the main visual shortfalls are the missing beige gradient background, the incomplete plot frame, and a possible runtime dependency on an unlisted hidePopup() scaffold function.
action_items: Fill the plot area with the source's cream/tan gradient background (e.g., via a chartArea background plugin) so the figure matches the original at a glance.
Draw top and right border lines to complete the full rectangular plot frame the source shows.

Guard the hidePopup() call in applyStep (e.g., `if (typeof hidePopup === 'function') hidePopup();`) — the scaffold documents showPopup/showTooltip/hideTooltip but not hidePopup, so stepping back to step 1 could throw and freeze the step player.
Nudge the step-2/3 '≈ 3 : 1' / '³⁵Cl : ³⁷Cl' bracket text a bit further right/up so it cannot crowd the 'M (64)' label near the top of the chart.
